scope: Correct marketing visuals that implied the same Swift code produces different-looking apps. No engine, release, legal, physical-device or GA qualification.

tools.browser: Google Chrome 155.0.8059.82 headless via DevTools protocol

finding: Earlier revisions drew the iPhone with iOS layout conventions and the Android phone with Material 3 layout, colors and a floating action button, so identical code appeared to yield two different apps. That contradicted the product goal of one codebase producing the same app on both platforms.
changes: Both hero phones and both workflow preview phones render one shared app design; only device hardware differs.
Platform section renamed 'One codebase. Same app.' with identical iOS and Android panels beside the shared declarations.
Hero, platform and demo copy now say 'the same app' instead of 'each platform's own controls' or 'two native experiences'.
open_question: mixer-product-plan.md section 8.3 asks adapters to keep platform idioms and says pixel-identical rendering is not the correctness criterion. The site now depicts one identical app design; whether the plan should commit to that appearance is a product decision for the user.
limitations: No public domain or production deployment; preview remains noindex.
Device, editor and control renderings are illustrations, not screenshots of Mixer-built apps.
Physical phones remain disconnected; no GA gate or reviewer acceptance changed.
